guidelines.fragment_description: A Class represents a blueprint of objects containing attributes and operations specific to the object type it models.
An Association represents a relationship between two classes, indicating that objects of one class can be related to objects of the other class through a defined link.
An Aggregation represents a whole-part relationship between two classes where one class is a container and the other class is a part.
A Composition represents a strong whole-part relationship between two classes, indicating that the part cannot exist independently of the whole.
A Generalization represents an inheritance relationship between a more general superclass and more specific subclasses.
A Realization defines a relationship where a class implements the behavior specified by an interface.
A Dependency indicates that a change in one class (supplier) may require changes to the other class (client).
An Interface defines a set of operations that specify a contract for implementing classes but contains no implementation itself.
An Attribute is a stored property or data value of a class, representing characteristics shared by all instances of the class.
An Operation is a function or service that a class can provide, representing behavior of the objects within the class.
